summary: This lecture tells of the companions' migration to Abyssinia in the fifth year of prophethood. After recalling the torture of Bilal, Khabbab, the family of Yasir and Mus'ab, the ustaz explains that the Prophet SAW looked for a safe place as a plan B and named a just Christian king, An-Najashi (Ashamah), across the Red Sea. The ustaz explains the three conditions of a companion, then the story of Layla packing and Umar's sympathy. About sixteen went first including Ruqayyah and Uthman, followed by a larger group led by Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. Quraysh sent Amr ibn al-As with gifts, but Najashi heard both sides, was moved to tears by Ja'far's recitation of Surah Maryam, and refused to hand anyone over. Najashi later believed and the Prophet SAW prayed the funeral prayer for him in absentia.
keyPoints: The Prophet SAW told the companions to migrate to Abyssinia because its king, An-Najashi, was a just Christian.
A companion is someone who met the Prophet SAW, believed and died as a Muslim.
About sixteen went first quietly at night, including Ruqayyah and Uthman, then about a hundred more.
Amr ibn al-As brought gifts to persuade Najashi to hand them over, but Najashi refused after hearing Ja'far.
Najashi wept hearing Surah Maryam, confirmed Ja'far's words on Isa and believed. The Prophet SAW prayed for him in absentia.

chapters.title: Opening and recap of Ramadan
chapters.summary: The ustaz begins with Najashi's decision, then welcomes pupils after Ramadan and recalls the special classes.

chapters.title: Recap of the torture of the companions
chapters.summary: The ustaz recalls Mus'ab, Suhaib, Khabbab, Bilal and the family of Yasir, and counts that it is the fifth year of the call.

chapters.title: Plan B
chapters.summary: Over a hundred had believed. The Prophet SAW grieved to see them tortured and sought a plan B so Islam would live on.

chapters.title: Surah Al-Kahf and Az-Zumar
chapters.summary: Surah Al-Kahf about the People of the Cave who fled to a cave and Az-Zumar saying Allah's earth is wide came down at this time.

chapters.title: An-Najashi and Abyssinia
chapters.summary: Najashi was a title, his name Ashamah, a just Christian king of Abyssinia across the Red Sea from the Hijaz.

chapters.title: Three conditions of a companion
chapters.summary: A companion is one who met the Prophet SAW, believed and died as a Muslim. Abu Jahal and Abu Lahab were not companions.

chapters.title: Layla and Umar
chapters.summary: Layla was packing to migrate and Umar, not yet Muslim, asked, sympathised and wished her a safe journey.

chapters.title: The first migration
chapters.summary: About sixteen went to Jeddah quietly at night including Ruqayyah and Uthman, Mus'ab, Ja'far and Asma'.

chapters.title: Quraysh send Amr ibn al-As
chapters.summary: After the second group, Quraysh sent the debater Amr ibn al-As with costly gifts to demand their return.

chapters.title: The just king hears both sides
chapters.summary: The just Najashi would not follow only one side and summoned the Muslims to speak.

chapters.title: Ja'far is chosen as spokesman
chapters.summary: The companions chose Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and did not prostrate to the king because they prostrate only to Allah.

chapters.title: Ja'far's speech
chapters.summary: Ja'far prepared his speech: we were ignorant, worshipping idols, eating carrion and oppressing the weak, then Allah sent Muhammad from among us.

chapters.title: Surah Maryam
chapters.summary: Najashi asked for a Quran recitation, and Ja'far recited Surah Maryam so beautifully that Najashi wept until his beard was wet.

chapters.title: Najashi refuses to hand them over
chapters.summary: Najashi said he would not hand anyone over. Amr tried again next day by questioning their view of Isa.

chapters.title: Isa and the line in the ground
chapters.summary: Ja'far said Isa is a prophet and servant of Allah, a noble Spirit born without a father. Najashi drew a line with a stick, confirmed it and returned the gifts.

chapters.title: Najashi dies and Q&A
chapters.summary: Najashi believed and died in Abyssinia, and the Prophet SAW prayed for him in absentia. The ustaz answers why the Prophet did not migrate to Abyssinia.

dalil.context: The ustaz says Allah told them the earth is wide, so they could leave Mecca and prostrate to Allah anywhere.
dalil.translation: Say, ‘[God says], believing servants, be mindful of your Lord! Those who do good in this world will have a good reward- God’s earth is wide––and those who persevere patiently will be given a full and unstinting reward.’

dalil.context: He neither begets nor is born.
dalil.translation: He begot no one nor was He begotten.
The Prophet SAW told the companions that in Abyssinia there was a just Christian king and that whoever wished could go and live there.
dalil.context: The ustaz relates the Prophet's words. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: Jibril told the Prophet SAW that Najashi had died and he and the companions prayed the funeral prayer for him in absentia in Madinah.
dalil.context: The ustaz narrates this event. He does not name a narrator or source.

people.role: The just Christian king of Abyssinia
people.context: Received the companions, wept at Surah Maryam, refused to hand them over and believed.

people.role: A female companion packing to migrate
people.context: Seen by Umar while packing, she thought Umar might embrace Islam.
Persecuted Muslims but sympathised and prayed for Layla's safety.
Migrated to Abyssinia with his wife.
Migrated to Abyssinia with her husband Uthman.

people.role: Leader and spokesman of the group
people.context: The Prophet's cousin who spoke before Najashi and recited Surah Maryam.
Sent with costly gifts to ask Najashi to return the Muslims but failed.
Sent Amr ibn al-As to Abyssinia.
Ja'far explained he is a servant and messenger of Allah born without a father.
Ja'far recited the surah about her, which touched Najashi's heart.
Did not migrate to Madinah as she died when he was 50 and was buried in Mecca.
Stayed in Mecca with her husband Abul As until after the Battle of Badr.

sirah.era: The fifth year of prophethood: migration to Abyssinia
sirah.summary: This lecture covers the first migration to Abyssinia, the Quraysh delegation and the hearing before Najashi.

events.label: Migration
events.title: Sixteen companions migrate
events.desc: They crossed the Red Sea from Jeddah at night.

events.label: Delegation
events.title: Amr ibn al-As brings gifts
events.desc: Quraysh sent him to ask Najashi to return the Muslims.

events.label: Spokesman
events.title: Ja'far is chosen to speak
events.desc: They chose Ja'far ibn Abi Talib to speak before the king.

events.label: Maryam
events.title: Ja'far recites Surah Maryam
events.desc: Najashi wept until his beard was wet.

events.label: Refusing
events.title: Najashi refuses to hand over
events.desc: He said he would return no one.

events.label: Isa
events.title: Ja'far explains about Isa
events.desc: Najashi confirmed Ja'far's words by drawing a line in the ground.

events.label: In absentia
events.title: Funeral prayer in absentia for Najashi
events.desc: The Prophet SAW and the companions prayed for him in Madinah.

lessons.title: Hearing both sides before judging
lessons.body: A just king does not follow one side only even when given gifts.

lessons.title: Bribery does not change justice
lessons.body: Najashi returned all of Amr's gifts.

lessons.title: Protecting the oppressed
lessons.body: Najashi refused to hand over the Muslims seeking protection.

lessons.title: Preparing before speaking
lessons.body: Ja'far arranged his speech so the king would understand and be convinced.

lessons.title: Choosing a fitting recitation
lessons.body: Ja'far chose Surah Maryam because Najashi was a Christian who revered Maryam.

lessons.title: Prostrating only to Allah
lessons.body: The companions did not prostrate to the king because prostration is for Allah alone.

lessons.title: Preparing a plan B
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW placed companions in a safe place so Islam would not stop.

lessons.title: A tender heart receives the Quran
lessons.body: Najashi wept hearing the beautiful Quran recitation.

lessons.title: Migration awaits Allah's command
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW would not migrate unless Allah gave a specific command.

glossary.meaning: One who met the Prophet SAW, believed and died as a Muslim.
The title of the king of Abyssinia, like the title Pharaoh. The king's name was Ashamah.
The old name of the region where Mecca lies in Saudi Arabia.
The sea between the Hijaz and Africa crossed by the companions.
Someone skilled at convincing others in debate.
The funeral prayer for someone who died far away.
The African land across the Red Sea, now Ethiopia and Eritrea.
